name: Hélias de Saint-Yrieix
summary:
Hélias de Saint-Yrieix was a French Benedictine abbot, papal judiciary official, bishop and Cardinal who played a pivotal role in shaping Western Europe's ecclesiastical politics during the 14th century.

As papal legate to France from 1337 until his death in 1367, Hélias de Saint-Yrieix worked closely with King Philip VI to implement reforms within the French Catholic Church. His efforts contributed significantly to the development of a more centralized and bureaucratic church structure.

De Saint-Yrieix's influence extended beyond ecclesiastical politics, as he was also a key figure in the diplomatic relations between France and the Holy Roman Empire during this period. He played a crucial role in resolving several border disputes between the two powers, which helped maintain peace in Western Europe for several decades.

De Saint-Yrieix's legacy can be seen in the continued development of papal authority within the Catholic Church, as well as his impact on French politics and diplomacy during the 14th century. His contributions to these fields have had a lasting impact on the course of Western European history.

In the world of art, de Saint-Yrieix's name is still remembered today for his patronage of several notable artists and architects of the time, including the famous French architect Pierre de Chelles.
